newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr on large capital flows.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends up vs dlr on large capital flows.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended up against the dollar on Tuesday on the back of large dollar sale by exporters and good inward remittances, dealers said.
Dealers have of late said they noticed a reluctance on the part of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to intervene aggressively in the forex market for fear of its impact on the domestic money market.
"RBI did not buy at earlier levels today," said a dealer, referring to the central bank's earlier dollar purchases at 35.84/85 levels.
RBI bought at 35.81/82 rupees to a dollar on Tuesday.
The rupee rose on the forward dollar market, reflecting RBI's initiatives in its 1997/98 (April-March) credit policy to prompt a cut in banks' lending rates.
"It was by and large discounted, but still had its impact," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay.
The six month annualised forward premium closed Tuesday at 5.75 percent compared with the previous close of 6.19 percent.
